Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: In the RCT, vitamin C supplementation did not affect mood, including depression.
Sentence: "The vitamin C supplementation did not affect mood and serum concentrations of BDNF."
Measured as: depression (mood status)
Population: Healthy subjects with inadequate serum vitamin C (<50 μmol/L), n = 46
Intervention: Vitamin C 500 mg twice a day for 4 weeks
Comparator: Placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 260
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Women from minority ethnic groups were less likely than white British women to be diagnosed with depression in primary care.
Sentence: "Women from minority ethnic groups were less likely to be diagnosed with depression in primary care compared with white British women (adjusted OR 0.66 (0.55-0.79) p<0.001), and black women were more likely to have a SMI (adjusted OR 2.79 (2.13-3.64) p<0.001)."
Measured as: diagnosis of depression in primary care
Population: Women aged 15-40 in contact with secondary mental health services and age-matched comparison women, Lambeth, London
Intervention: No intervention; exposure is minority ethnicity (not vitamin D)
Comparator: White British women
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 18,349
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported
